{"data":{"id":"1324733","key":"ENG-4070","fields":{"summary":"Foot Locker - Excel Export not exporting Data - Looping back to Login Screen","description":"

MM SRE notes

This issue seems to be caused by a bug in ClientSlug mode:

Since the Download link's domain differs, they get redirected to the sign on page → seems like the cookie is stamped as ‘Host-only'

For the fix we could either stamp the cookies with a shared parent or change the behaviour to use relative urls.

When clicking on download from the notifications to download your exported data, the menu flickers and loops you back to the logon screen. Sometimes it downloads the data quickly before the logout, but others it does not download at all and just completely signs you out.

Please see video below for reference.

Working as expected. Test case
Foot Locker users in ClientSlug mode clicking the "download" link from an Excel-export notification get bounced to the login screen instead of receiving the file — the menu flickers, occasionally a partial download starts before being
interrupted, then the user is fully logged out. Cloned from production incident RCS-27169 (Closed, High); High
priority Bug.

Root Cause

Cross-domain cookie scoping in ClientSlug mode.

The export-download notification's link points at a different domain/subdomain than the one that issued the auth
cookie:

  • Auth cookie was stamped on the session's primary host (e.g. <env>.apprissretail.com/<slug>/platform/...) as
    host-only (no explicit parent Domain= attribute).

  • The download link in the notification was generated against a different domain (the SRE screenshot confirms this —
    "the Download link's domain differs").

  • The browser does not send a host-only cookie to a different host, so the request to the download endpoint arrives
    with no auth cookie.

  • The auth middleware sees an unauthenticated request and 302-redirects to the sign-on page — i.e. the "logout"/"loop
    back to login" symptom.

The mechanism is therefore not a Secure platform code bug — it's a configuration interaction: ClientSlug mode
(per-tenant slug-based URL form, see e.g. Sources/Core/Core/Util/UriHelpers and the PlatformUrlScheme.ClientSlug
branch we touched in ENG-3261) routes the user under one host pattern, while the per-tenant arpfiles config that
drives notification/download link generation was outputting a link with a different host. Once those two diverge, the
host-only cookie cannot follow.

The SRE wrote the precise mechanism into the ticket: "the Download link's domain differs, they get redirected to the
sign on page → seems like the cookie is stamped as 'Host-only'."

When Introduced

  • Locality: the fix-causing change lives in arpfiles (per-client config repo at C:\\arpfiles), not in C:\\Secure. git
    log --all --grep="ENG-4070" in C:\\Secure returns nothing — no Secure-side commit was needed.

  • Context: introduced as part of the Platform Unification (PU) rollout for Foot Locker (the Implementation Notes
    explicitly say "Reverted the arpfiles to what they were supposed before PU"). The PU work changed the URL form for
    Foot Locker, but the arpfiles entry driving export-notification download URLs was not adjusted to match — it kept
    emitting a link on the legacy/different host.

  • Commit SHA: lives in the arpfiles repo, which the analyze-ticket skill's git commands are scoped to C:\\Secure for.
    The actual arpfiles commit needs to be located by your delivery/SRE team in C:\\arpfiles (git log --grep="ENG-4070"
    there should surface the revert commit).

  • Originating ticket: clone of RCS-27169 (Foot Locker customer-reported production incident, Closed).

Why It Was Introduced

During Foot Locker's Platform Unification migration, someone touched the arpfiles config that determines the
host/domain used in export-notification download URLs (probably to align with PU URL semantics elsewhere, or because a
template was copied from a SubDomain-mode tenant). The change went in for what looked like consistency, but Foot
Locker is on ClientSlug mode — so the new download URL pattern produced a host different from the session-cookie's
host, breaking auth on download requests.

This sits inside the same systemic risk family as ENG-3261 (BBW report notification URLs using /secure/ instead of
/platform/ in PC mode): a per-client URL/host config divergence that only surfaces for one URL-scheme variant.
ENG-3261 fixed the platform-side code so users on each scheme get a link in their own scheme; ENG-4070 fixes it the
other direction by reverting the arpfiles entry so it stops emitting the wrong host for Foot Locker's ClientSlug mode.

Systemic Risk Note

Two patterns to watch:

  1. PU-era arpfiles changes that introduced cross-domain/cross-subdomain links for ClientSlug-mode tenants. Foot Locker
    isn't unique — any other ClientSlug-mode tenant whose arpfiles entries were modified during PU may have the same
    latent issue for any flow that returns a link in a notification, email, or async-job result (export downloads,
    attachment links, report URLs, share-this links). Worth a sweep: for each ClientSlug tenant, audit arpfiles entries
    that emit fully-qualified URLs and confirm the host matches the tenant's session host.

  2. Host-only auth cookies vs. cross-subdomain links. The auth cookies in this codebase are stamped host-only (no
    parent Domain=). Anywhere the platform generates a fully-qualified link to a different host within the same tenant,
    that link won't carry auth — same failure mode as this bug. The two suggested directions in the SRE notes ("stamp the
    cookies with a shared parent or change the behaviour to use relative urls") would both eliminate the entire risk
    family; the chosen Foot Locker fix only patches this one tenant's config. If the customer touches another PU-era
    client and a similar download flow misfires, expect the same root cause.

Cross-reference: ENG-3261 is the closest prior — same flavour of per-client URL-form mismatch between code/config and
the user's actual session host. The fix style there was code-side (per-user Platform.UrlScheme tracking +
UriHelpers.GetExternalApplicationAddress); the fix style here is config-side (revert). The two approaches address
overlapping symptom families.

Fix Direction

The applied fix is config-only: revert the Foot Locker arpfiles entry that emits the export-notification download URL
back to its pre-PU value (the URL form that matches Foot Locker's actual session host). Per Implementation Notes:
"Reverted the arpfiles to what they were supposed before PU."

Status: In Testing (you are the QA owner). The validation target is on Foot Locker test environment — run an Excel
export, wait for the notification, click the download link, confirm the file downloads on the first click rather than
redirecting to the sign-on page.

Two follow-ups worth filing, both pre-existing risks that this revert doesn't address:

  1. Audit all ClientSlug-mode tenants' arpfiles for similar PU-era host changes that might break
    notification/email/async-result URLs (see Systemic Risk #1).

  2. Decide on the long-term fix suggested by SRE: either stamp auth cookies with a shared parent Domain= (eliminates
    the host-only constraint for all cross-subdomain links in this tenant family) or migrate notification-emitted URLs to
    relative paths so they inherit the request host (eliminates the cross-domain mismatch entirely). The current
    per-tenant config revert is a stop-gap; either of these systemic fixes would prevent the next tenant from hitting the
    same bug.
